source_topic: Second list #78: Model Agreement as a Scientific Instrument
title: Can cross-model disagreement serve as an empirical uncertainty instrument in breast-tumor diagnosis?
question: Do disagreements among diverse, independently trained classifiers identify predictions at elevated error risk and enable safer selective prediction?
dataset: UCI Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer (WDBC), 569 samples, 30 features
validation: Repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation, 20 repeats (100 held-out folds); all preprocessing fit inside each training fold
primary_metric: Error enrichment among the top disagreement quintile relative to remaining predictions
secondary_metric: Error rate after abstaining on the top disagreement quintile versus error rate on all predictions

all_required: selective error reduction >= 25% after abstaining on top disagreement quintile
bootstrap 95% confidence interval lower bound for enrichment > 1.0

failure_policy: If any required gate fails, classify as negative and preserve full outputs; do not produce a success paper.
